spec.material: one section of a take-home revision pack: the mathematics of one lesson objective, explained, worked through and practised
spec.audience: {reader} who sat in this lesson and is revising alone at home
requirements: Speak directly to the learner about the mathematics, never about the lesson as an event: no mention of the teacher or what happened in class, no lesson step or objective labels, no mention of where any material came from.
Write your own learner-facing section title; nothing in the inputs is a heading for the reader.

Teach the objective inside this lesson's topic and subtopic: examples and practice must be of the kind the topic names (a lesson on algebraic expressions practises on algebraic terms, not on bare numbers).
Every practice question must have its answer in the section, so the learner attempts first and then checks.
Never refer to a picture, space, partner or answer key that is not in the pack itself.
Explain the objective in full: the rule or idea, why it holds, an instance with numbers, and the slip learners most often make.
Give at least two worked examples, the second harder than the first, and at least three practice questions that each ask something different.
Every rule, worked answer and practice answer is correct; test each rule on numbers of your own before stating it.

parts.name: title
parts.description: The section's heading for the learner, in your own words

parts.name: explanation
parts.description: The principle, relationship, rule or representation the learner needs to review this objective: concise and relational, not a summary of the topic

parts.name: figures
parts.description: Labelled drawings from the lesson that this objective uses, in the order the explanation and examples use them

fields.name: caption
fields.description: What the drawing shows, naming its labelled points

fields.name: drawing
fields.description: One tikzpicture environment that draws it, with the same labels

parts.name: worked_examples
parts.description: Worked examples of what the objective teaches, from simple to harder, each solved line by line

fields.name: solution
fields.description: The solution, one line of working at a time

fields.name: working
fields.description: One line of the working, in LaTeX between $ signs; plain text in a lesson that does not calculate, such as naming kinds of words

fields.name: commentary
fields.description: Why this line follows, in one short sentence

parts.name: practice
parts.description: Questions the learner attempts alone, each with the answer it is checked against

fields.name: question
fields.description: The question, as the learner reads it, with no answer or hint to the answer in it

fields.name: answer
fields.description: The answer the learner checks against after attempting

fields.name: worked_solution
fields.description: The steps to the answer, where the answer alone would not show the learner what to do
